scenes.text: Seven witnesses saw the killer's face. Not one of them could describe it. Because in this city... nobody has a face.
It rains here most nights. Under an umbrella, every man looks the same. I'm the one they call when that becomes a problem.
You'd think crimes get solved with faces, fingerprints, and witnesses. Here, our hands are lines, our faces are circles... and every witness describes everyone.
So when the rain murders began, the department gave up fast. Four victims. Four rainy nights. One burnt match beside every body.
But here's what the academy never teaches. People can hide their faces. Nobody can hide their habits.
The killer only worked in the rain. Always at seven minutes past three. Like he was keeping an appointment.
Every match was torn from the left side of the book. He was left- handed. That narrowed it down to half the city.
His footprints told me more. Short step, long step. He walked with a limp. Now it was a quarter of the city.
One witness remembered something. Not a face. A color. In a sea of umbrellas... one was red.
Then I found the thread. All four victims sat on the jury that freed the Holloway killer. The man who murdered my partner.
Someone was finishing what the court wouldn't. I chased that red umbrella through every alley in town. All I ever caught was a warm match.
One juror was left. Friday, the forecast said rain. So I parked outside her building, and watched the clock crawl toward three- oh- seven.
I blinked. Just once. Then I was standing in the rain. Her window was dark. And a burnt match was cooling in my left hand.
Rain. Three- oh- seven. A left hand. A limp. A red umbrella by my own door. I'd spent months drawing the killer's portrait. It was a mirror.
The blue lights came seven minutes later. My own precinct. I didn't run. Where do you run, when the man you're chasing... is you?
They put me in the lineup. The witness couldn't see my face. She didn't need to. She watched me walk.
Case closed. Except... habits can be learned. Copied. Worn like a mask. And outside, it was still raining.
In a city without faces, the hardest one to see is your own. So you tell me. Was I the killer... or the perfect suspect?
